subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.**

I hate to __get off on the wrong foot__.

options.text: To start something with positive factors
To start something with neutral factors
To start a relationship or activity badly
To start something with an injury on the wrong foot

solution:
The correct answer is **'To start a relationship or activity badly'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom** "get off on the wrong foot"** in the given sentence is: **To start a relationship or activity badly.**
 
• Explanation: When someone says they **"hate to get off on the wrong foot,"** it means they dislike starting something in a negative or unfavorable manner. It suggests a desire to begin on good terms or with positive circumstances.
 
• In this context, the speaker expresses **a reluctance to begin a relationship or activity in a negative way.**
